title: UPT Atlas Record
description: Versioned JSON artifact for a Phase 0 atlas family (`src/atlas`): the models, the bridges between them, and the claimed bridges that were rejected. DOCUMENTATION ONLY — this tree carries no JSON-Schema validator and adds no dependency to get one; the schema exists so an external validator can check an emitted record and so the field set has one written source. `schemaVersion` is independent of `packageVersion`. Experimental — does not imply public API stability. TypeScript sources (`src/atlas/types.ts`) remain authoritative for in-memory types, and Phase 0 pilot types are replaced rather than migrated (Atlas-Phase-0-Design.md §4).

schemaVersion.description: Record major version. Parsers reject unknown incompatible majors. Additive optional fields do not require a bump.

packageVersion.description: `package.json` version of the UPT build that emitted the record. Independent of `schemaVersion`.

family.description: Identifier of the atlas family this record describes (Phase 0 emits a single family).

models.description: The models that are bridge endpoints. Ids must be unique within the record.

bridges.description: Asserted relations between models, each with premises and a conclusion.

rejections.description: Claimed bridges that do NOT hold, retained with the counterexample that defeats each one. A rejection is evidence, not an omission.

limitCharacter.description: Whether the limit taken by the relation is regular or singular.

evidenceTag.description: One derived evidence tag (`ALL_EVIDENCE_TAGS` in `src/relations/types.ts`, in declaration order). `formally-proved` is reachable only through a reviewed formal reference of kind `bridge`; `symbolically-checked` and `numerically-supported` only through a witness the committed results record as checked.

approximationBound.description: Quantitative error bound. `horizon` (prose) states where the approximation stops being usable; the machine predicate that decides it lives in the TypeScript source and is not serialisable, so only the prose form appears here.

K.description: Multiplicative constant of the bound, in the stated norm.

delta.description: Small parameter the bound is expressed in.

norm.description: The norm the bound is stated in. A bound without its norm is not a bound: an equivalence can be an isometry in one norm and not in another (§9).

domain.description: Region of parameter and state space where the bound is claimed.

horizon.description: Prose statement of the time or regime past which the bound no longer holds.

parameterRange.description: Optional prose range of the parameter the bound was taken over.

uniformity.description: What the error is uniform in. null or an empty array means not yet analysed; boundPath then returns no numeric bound.

deltaAtBasis.description: What the machine form `deltaAt` (TypeScript only, not serialisable) rests on: `closed-form` returns the exact error; `numerically-supported` returns a value a witness checked. Present on every approximation bound.

witness.description: A named check that supports a record, and the test file that runs it (the TS `Witness` type). The emitted record carries no prose description: the id, the kind, the test path and the stated tolerance are the witness.

counterexample.description: A concrete instance that defeats a claimed relation.

params.description: Parameter assignment at which the claim fails.

canonicalRefs.description: Ids into `CANONICAL_EQUATIONS`. A ref that does not resolve is a test failure, not a warning (§3).

atlasBridge.description: An asserted relation. The if/then below encodes the Phase 0 rule that an approximation without an error bound is an assertion rather than a relation: when `relation` is `approximation`, `bound` is required and `bound.horizon` with it.

premises.description: Model ids the relation reasons FROM.

conclusion.description: Model id the relation reasons TO.

evidence.description: The evidence tags the claim DERIVES (`deriveEvidence`, against `data/atlas/witness-results.json`), sorted. Never stored on a record; `toAtlasJson` computes it at write time.

normTransports.description: Optional, on an exact-equivalence bridge only: per-direction declarations of how the map carries an error norm (docs/planning/ADR-transported-norm-composition.md). A bound crosses the map only in a norm and direction declared here, with its own witness.

claimedRelation.description: The relation that was claimed and does not hold.

conclusion.description: Model id the claim reached, or null when the claim has no surviving conclusion.
